name: Task
description: Represents a single task running on the system. The Task object is a member of the Tasks collection. The Tasks collection includes all the applications that are currently running on the system.
remarks: Use Tasks (Index), where Index is the application name or the index number, to return a single Task object. The following example switches to and resizes the application window for the first visible task in the Tasks collection. The following example restores the Calculator application window if Calculator is in the Tasks collection. Use Visual Basic's Shell function to run an executable program and add the program to the Tasks collection.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Word application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which the specified object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the parent object of the specified Task object.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Returns the name of the specified object. Read-only String.

properties.name: Left
properties.description: Returns or sets a Long that represents the horizontal position of the specified task, measured in points. Read/write.

properties.name: Top
properties.description: Returns or sets the vertical position, in points, of the specified window. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Width
properties.description: Returns or sets the width of the specified Task object, in points. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Height
properties.description: Returns or sets the height of the specified task window. Read/write Long.

properties.name: WindowState
properties.description: Returns or sets the state of the specified document window or task window. Read/write WdWindowState.

properties.name: Visible
properties.description: True if the specified object is visible. Read/write Boolean.

parameters.name: Wait
parameters.description: True to wait until the user has activated Word before activating the task. False to immediately activate the task, even if Word isn't active.

methods.name: Move
methods.signature: Move(Left As Long, Top As Long)

parameters.name: Left
parameters.description: The horizontal screen position of the specified window.

parameters.name: Top
parameters.description: The vertical screen position of the specified window.

methods.name: Resize
methods.signature: Resize(Width As Long, Height As Long)

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The width of the window, in points.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The height of the window, in points.

methods.name: SendWindowMessage
methods.signature: SendWindowMessage(Message As Long, wParam As Long, lParam As Long)
methods.description: Sends a Windows message and its associated parameters to the specified task.

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: A hexadecimal number that corresponds to the message you want to send. If you have the Microsoft Platform Software Development Kit, you can look up the name of the message in the header files (Winuser.h, for example) to find the associated hexadecimal number (precede the hexadecimal value with &h).

parameters.name: wParam
parameters.description: Parameters appropriate for the message you are sending. For information about what these values represent, see the reference topic for that message in the documentation included with the Microsoft Platform Software Development Kit, available on MSDN. To retrieve the appropriate values, you may need to use the Spy tool (which comes with the kit).
